candidate1/12026-09-01On large-cap tech in a low-vol bull regime, volume contraction alone is not a distribution signal — the manager's insistence on a volume-confirmed-distribution standard before acting on the bear thesis was the decisive correct call, and the firm should codify that threshold explicitly so it isn't re-litigated on every quiet week. The slow-leak fallback stop (3 closes below the 50-day regardless of volume) is the kind of asymmetric risk adjustment that should be the default on any structural-trend position where the primary stop is volume-conditional, not an exception requiring a risk team override. Sizing at ¼ slot pending data verification was appropriately conservative given the modest +2.44% payoff; the binding constraint on this name is confirmation quality, not conviction.
candidate0/02026-09-01When a name already carries a meaningfully bearish fundamental tilt (here a 21% forward P/E premium plus near-zero FFC yield), the "no confirmed volume signal" doctrine and a 20-session time-stop are both calibrated too loosely for that starting position — the 2.69% drift in five days shows the bleed was already in motion without needing a volume-confirmed distribution spike to be "real." Next time, scale the time-stop or the signal bar to the magnitude of the existing fundamental tilt: a neutral name can afford 20 sessions of patience, but a name with a double-digit valuation premium warrants a shorter window or an alternative exit criterion that doesn't require a volume event to trigger.
candidate0/02026-09-01The manager cited AMD's 29.5x forward multiple as leaving "no cushion for a narrative wobble" to justify not buying, yet then deployed the AAPL calm-regime lesson (contracted volume = no distribution signal = don't short) to block the short thesis. The error is the asymmetric treatment of that same valuation fragility: a name priced for perfection is vulnerable to a wobble in both directions, so "no cushion" should argue against holding full size or initiating long *and* lower the bar for the short, not only for the long. The AAPL sub-SMA50 dip lesson does not transfer to high-multiple, narrative-dependent semis, where "calm regime" is often the precursor to the wobble rather than a shield against it.
candidate0/02026-09-01The "symmetric block" logic (data gap blocks both long and short conviction equally) is only valid when choosing a fresh entry; when you already hold a long position, the relevant comparison is "hold existing long" vs. "reduce or exit," and the data gap undermines the justification for continuing to carry that exposure. A 20-session SMA20 clock is too slow a trigger when the stock can bleed ~3% in a week — the temporal stop should be calibrated to the speed at which the base-drift failure mode actually materializes, not to a comfortable re-evaluation window.
candidate0/02026-09-01The manager's reliance on the AAPL "sub-SMA50 dips without SMA200 break are mean-reversion" lesson led him to anchor the stop at a structural level 3.3% below entry, but in a low-coverage name where he himself conceded a catalyst arrives with zero warning, that distance makes the stop functionally irrelevant within the holding window—it protects against a regime change, not against the exact scenario he identified. When the data gap is the stated reason to withhold a long-side conviction, the symmetric application is to withhold a short-side conviction from pure technicals alone. On AAPL specifically, a sub-SMA20 dip without cap flow or short-interest confirmation has a high baseline probability of being a 3–5-day reclaim, which is exactly what happened here.
active3/02026-08-24When the manager's own rationale simultaneously asserts "structurally intact uptrend" and "confirmed near-term weakness" (price below SMA50 but well above SMA200), the weakness is a mean-reversion dip, not distribution — especially with binary catalysts pending. The trim was driven by the near-term weakness signal while the stronger structural signals (SMA200, 3-month momentum, catalyst asymmetry) all pointed the opposite direction; the correct resolution of that tension in a name like AAPL is to treat SMA50 pullbacks as non-signal or light-buy, not as trim triggers. Next time, require the "near-term weakness" to also break SMA200 or show volume-confirmed distribution (consecutive down days with rising volume) before it carries enough weight to override the structural case.
